title: ClimbPayload
description: Canonical wire-format payload (v3, packed) sent from the Android companion app to the Garmin Connect IQ apps over the Communications API. Uses short keys and packed integer arrays to minimise bytes. Produced by service/ClimbPayloadBuilder; consumed by the hand-written Monkey C parsers (garmin*/source/CommListener.mc and garmin-surface/source/SurfaceData.mc). protocol/examples/*.json are canonical wire samples; ProtocolRoundTripTest validates both the examples and the live builder output against this schema.

v.description: Wire schema version. Consumers reject any value other than 3.

mode.description: 'route' = follow a single route (climbs carry sd/ed); 'radius' = nearby climbs (climbs carry slat/slon).

routeId.description: Stable route identifier (route mode). Absent in radius mode.

name.description: Optional user/display name for the route. Only emitted when <= 32 chars.

pal.description: Optional color palette (issue #258): 1 = colorblind-friendly palette (pale yellow + light-to-dark blue ramp for the six colorIndex values, blue/orange status colors instead of green/red); absent = default yellow-to-red palette. Only the rendered colors change: colorIndex values in segs/zc and their gradient buckets are identical in both palettes. A phone setting; route, single-climb and radius payloads. Consumers treat any other value as the default palette.

un.description: Optional display-unit bitmask (issue #262), any mode: bit 1 = imperial distance/elevation/speed (mi/ft/mph), bit 2 = tyre pressure in psi, bit 4 = temperature in F. Absent or 0 = all metric. Only emitted when non-zero; watch parsers ignore unknown bits and treat a non-integer as metric. Display only: every other distance on the wire stays in metres.

rtl.description: Route mode (optional): total route length in whole metres. The watch derives distance-along-course as (rtl - Activity.Info.distanceToDestination) when navigating.

surfSec.description: Surface/named flat sections (route mode), sent in the lean surface-datafield payload (with climbs: []). Ordered by start distance.

climbs.description: Climbs. Route mode: ordered by sd. Radius mode: ordered closest-first.

hz.description: Route mode (optional, issue #203): hazard markers packed as [startM, endM, type, ...], 3 ints per hazard, ordered by startM. type 0 = road tunnel (OpenStreetMap, 'licht aan'), 1 = technical descent (steep or bendy, detected from the route geometry). Distances in whole metres from the route start. At most 32 hazards; omitted when none, and dropped when the payload would exceed the byte budget.

gh.description: Route mode (optional, issue #178): virtual opponent, the rider's own fastest earlier complete ride of this route, packed as [stepM, sec1, sec2, ..., secN]. stepM = metres per step (>= 250, coarser for long routes so N <= 100); sec_k = timer seconds that ride spent from (k-1)*stepM to min(k*stepM, rtl), so the last step may be shorter. Computed on the phone from Strava GPS tracks; the watch sums the steps, interpolates at the live route progress and shows seconds ahead/behind. Omitted when no ride covered the whole route, in radius mode and single-climb payloads, and dropped (after zc) when the payload would exceed the byte budget.

fss.description: Specialized starred flat segments (route mode), shown as a separate list section in the widget. Only segments with an assigned surface (t 0-4) are sent. Omitted when none qualify.

lay.description: Optional datafield stat-slot layout chosen in the phone app: 5 metric codes for [left, middle, right, row 4, bottom line] of the active-climb page. 0 remaining distance, 1 remaining elevation, 2 current-segment gradient, 3 climb average gradient, 4 VAM, 5 ETA, 6 ghost delta (vs PR/plan), 7 interval block, 8 speed, 9 heart rate, 10 power, 11 cadence, 12 elapsed time, 13 empty, 14 auto row 4 (block else VAM), 15 auto bottom (ghost else ETA). Omitted = default [0,1,2,14,15]. Both modes. The watch falls back to the default per slot for an unknown code and to the full default for a malformed array. Codes mirror domain/watch/WatchFieldLayout.java and garmin/source/FieldLayout.mc.

sd.description: Route mode: cumulative distance (m) along the route where the climb starts.

ed.description: Route mode: cumulative distance (m) along the route where the climb ends.

slat.description: Radius mode: climb start latitude as degrees x 100000 (integer).

slon.description: Radius mode: climb start longitude as degrees x 100000 (integer).

len.description: Climb length in metres. Domain rule: >= 800.

ag.description: Average gradient as fixed-point percent x 10 (7.2% -> 72).

n.description: Optional user/display name for the climb (<= 32 chars).

segs.description: Packed segments: [distance, elevationGain, gradientFixedPoint, colorIndex, ...], 4 ints per segment. gradientFixedPoint = percent x 10; colorIndex 0-5 (see colors.md).

calib.description: Route mode (optional): packed GPS calibration points [distanceFromClimbStart, latInt, lonInt, ...], 3 ints per point. latInt/lonInt = degrees x 100000.

surf.description: Optional: one surface-type code (0-5) per segment, parallel to segs. Omitted when all segments are UNKNOWN.

tsec.description: Route mode (optional): per-segment target time in whole seconds, one int per segment, parallel to segs. Manual, power-based pacing plan. Omitted when no pacing plan is available.

refsec.description: Route mode (optional): per-segment PR reference time in whole seconds, one int per segment, parallel to segs. The fastest previous split ever recorded on that exact segment (across all attempts, not necessarily the same attempt) — used to render a live 'ahead/behind your PR' delta. Distinct from 'tsec' (a manual pacing target); both may be present. Omitted when no attempt with a matching segment count exists.

vam.description: Optional: packed gradient-implied VAM (vertical ascent m/h) per segment: [avgVamMPerH, peakVamMPerH, ...], 2 ints per segment, parallel to segs. Derived from gradient at a fixed reference climbing speed (routes carry no elapsed-time data, so this is a planning estimate, not a measured ascent rate); peak is the steepest short window within the segment. Omitted unless every segment has a computed value.

ib.description: Optional interval block (issue #180): [targetWatts, lowWatts, highWatts], the power band to hold from the foot to the top of this climb. Computed on the phone from the block's % FTP and the rider's FTP. Omitted when the climb has no block or no FTP is set.

ev.description: Optional Everesting attempt on this climb (issue #217): [targetM, repeats, startLatInt, startLonInt, topLatInt, topLonInt], coordinates = degrees x 100000. The phone plans the repeats (ceil(target / elevation gain)); the watch counts summit passes near the top coordinate (re-armed near the start) and compares the activity's total ascent with targetM. At most one climb per payload; omitted when no attempt is planned or the climb has no calibration points.

zc.description: Optional (issue #66): per-segment FTP intensity-zone color, one colorIndex (0-5, see colors.md 'FTP intensity zones') per segment, parallel to segs. A second, optional color source next to the gradient colorIndex in segs, which stays the default: the watch uses zc only when its 'Kleurmodus' setting is FTP-zone. Computed on the phone from the rider's FTP and weights (estimated segment power -> Coggan zone -> colorIndex). Both modes; omitted without a complete rider profile, and dropped from any payload that would otherwise exceed the 4 KB budget.

s.description: Metres from route start where the segment begins.

e.description: Metres from route start where the segment ends (> s).

s.description: Metres from route start where the section begins.

e.description: Metres from route start where the section ends (> s).

cp.description: Packed GPS checkpoints [distanceFromRouteStart, latInt, lonInt, ...], 3 ints per checkpoint. latInt/lonInt = degrees x 100000. May be empty.
